### Fixed
- **The CLI bridge refreshes an expired token instead of asking for a login.** `muster agent --mcp-server` exposed only `authenticate_muster` whenever its access token had expired at start, although a refresh token was stored and `muster auth status` read the session as authenticated with weeks of auto-refresh left; a client on top of the bridge (`platformctl`, any MCP client using `call_tool`) failed with `tool 'call_tool' not found` until another muster command happened to refresh the token. The bridge now connects with the stored refresh token and the transport refreshes it on the first request; only a refresh the server refuses falls back to `authenticate_muster`. A refresh also keeps the ID token it returns: mcp-go's token type has no field for it, so every refresh stored the new access token next to the old ID token, and `muster auth status` told the person to log in again. An expired ID token next to a refresh token now reads `expired … ago (auto-refresh)`. ([#1298](https://github.com/giantswarm/muster/issues/1298))
